data.body:
IMPLEMENTED AND PUSHED — Gerrit change 1136 ("7c26: survive an issue moving project"), commit
431019b17 on branch jira-family-seam. Awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

WHAT LANDED, against the plan's Approach
 * `BindingStore.record_jira_id(local_id, jira_id)` + `get_jira_id(local_id)` — the capture and the
   accessor, ADDITIVE by construction.
 * `BindingStore.note_absent_or_rekey(jira_key, client)` — on a 404 it re-asks by the immutable
   numeric id; on a hit whose key DIFFERS it re-keys the binding, updates the reverse index in the
   SAME operation, resets the absence counter, persists, and emits a deduped `binding-rekeyed`
   alert. Returns True on a re-key, False when the absence was recorded exactly as before.
 * Module-level `_current_key_by_id(client, jira_id)` — reuses `get_issue_by_rest`, since
   `GET /rest/api/{2,3}/issue/{issueIdOrKey}` accepts an id wherever it accepts a key on BOTH
   deployments. So NO new transport member and no vendor branch was needed — which matters, because
   the DC transport is at 789 LOC against the 800 cap and had 11 lines of headroom.
 * Capture wired at `dispatch_one` create, in the SAME write that records the key, so the id and the
   key never disagree on disk. getattr-guarded so a store predating the member is a no-op rather
   than a persist-floor failure that would skip the create.
 * BOTH 404 paths wired: `outbound_differ._diff_one` (the primary one for a move — a moved issue
   leaves the project-scoped snapshot entirely) and `binding_walk`'s CONFIRMED_404 branch.

AC-BY-AC
 * "binding SURVIVES, re-keyed, test FAILS against current code" ->
   `test_a_moved_issue_keeps_its_binding_and_is_rekeyed`, driven END-TO-END through the real walk.
 * "absence probe does NOT retire an issue reachable by id" ->
   `test_the_absence_probe_does_not_retire_an_issue_reachable_by_id` with GRACE lowered to 1, so a
   single unrecovered 404 would retire.
 * "reverse index updated in the same operation" -> `test_the_reverse_index_follows_the_rekey`, plus
   `test_the_rekey_is_persisted_not_merely_in_memory` (re-read from disk).
 * "legacy bindings keep working, no migration" ->
   `test_a_legacy_binding_without_an_id_still_retires_at_grace`, which also asserts NO lookup is
   attempted when there is no id to ask by.
 * "id fallback NOT attempted while the key resolves" ->
   `test_the_id_fallback_is_not_attempted_while_the_key_resolves`.
 * "Cloud unchanged: no existing jira_key-taking method changes signature or semantics" ->
   `test_no_existing_jira_key_taking_method_changed_signature` pins ten signatures via
   `inspect.signature`. This is WHY the capture is a separate `record_jira_id` rather than a
   parameter on `bind_confirm`/`record_pending_key`.

Two cells beyond the ACs guard the fix's own failure mode — that a recovery could MASK a deletion:
`test_a_genuine_deletion_still_retires_even_with_a_captured_id` and
`test_an_unchanged_key_is_recorded_as_an_absence`. Every unproven case falls THROUGH to the
unchanged bookkeeping.

VERIFICATION
 * 13/13 new tests pass; 294 pass across the neighbouring suites (binding_walk, all of diffing/,
   absence lifecycle, binding_store).
 * MUTATION-CHECKED, three ways: reverting `binding_walk` to the pre-fix `note_absent` fails 4 cells
   with their intended messages; deleting the reverse-index maintenance fails exactly 2; deleting
   the `save()` fails exactly 1.
 * MY OWN ORACLE WAS WRONG FIRST TIME, and I record it because the lesson generalises: the stub
   probe 404'd on EVERY key, so after the re-key it also 404'd the NEW key — which the code
   correctly treats as a real absence and retires. The test was mis-specified, not the fix. The
   probe is now key-aware, matching what a move actually produces, with the reason in its docstring.
 * make lint + make typecheck clean (mypy: 399 files). All four touched modules under the 800 cap:
   binding_store 744, binding_walk 352, dispatch_one 796, outbound_differ 792.

TWO EXISTING TEST STUBS WERE UPDATED, preserving intent. `test_outbound_differ_bound_but_absent.py`
and `test_inbound_differ_bound_but_absent.py` define stub stores with `note_absent` only, so the
differ's new call found nothing and their "absence bumped once" assertions broke. Each stub now
implements `note_absent_or_rekey` delegating to `note_absent` — exactly the real store's degradation
contract when no id is captured — so the assertions keep their original meaning.

WHY outbound_differ WAS REFACTORED (it will look unrelated in the diff, so the reason is here):
that module sits at EXACTLY the locked 800-LOC cap on main, and it deliberately does NOT import the
concrete BindingStore (a documented Protocol boundary), so the wiring had to be local AND cost
lines. Three byte-identical getattr-guarded bookkeeping wrappers (`_note_absent`, `_clear_absent`,
`_set_last_get`) collapse into one `_best_effort(binding_store, member, *args)`. That bought the
lines from real duplication rather than from comments. No test referenced the three by name.

THE [operator-attested] AC — PARTIALLY SETTLED, AND THE UNSETTLED PART IS NOW A KNOWN NEGATIVE
The criterion asks what `GET /rest/api/2/issue/{oldKey}` returns for a MOVED issue on DC 8.17.1.
**It cannot be settled on this harness, and the reason is itself the finding:** a project move is
not performable through the authoritative client. Verified AT RUNTIME (not from docs) against the
installed pycontribs/jira 3.10.5 — it exposes no move member; `move_to_backlog` is Agile-backlog and
`move_version` is versions. DC's move is the UI wizard (`/secure/MoveIssue!default.jspa`, form-token
bound), and this repo forbids hand-rolled REST for DC. So 200-with-new-key vs 301 vs 404 stays open,
and I am recording that rather than picking the answer two research passes disagreed about.

What the live cells DO establish, added to `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_transport.py`:
 * `test_an_issue_resolves_by_its_immutable_numeric_id` — the fix's load-bearing mechanism: a by-id
   read answers with the issue's CURRENT key on a real instance. Had DC rejected an id here the
   whole fallback would be inert, and inert in the SILENT direction.
 * `test_a_deleted_issue_fails_by_key_AND_by_id_so_deletions_are_not_masked` — the live counterpart
   of the unit cell above.
These need a harness run to report; that evidence will be recorded here before this ticket closes.

The fix was deliberately designed to be correct under ALL THREE readings of the unsettled question,
which is exactly why it did not have to wait for the answer.
